_comment: Template for evidence/<run-id>/evidence.json. Every value here is a placeholder: fill each from the run, never invent one. Stage 13 on 8453 is the three vault unpauses only (issue 1520, rmUSDC added by issue 1710 because all three vaults deploy paused, rmAGENT is retired by ADR-0017): one govern entry per vault (unpause-USDC, unpause-PROTO, unpause-RWA), each with its own schedule tx, its own execute tx, its own timelock operation id (operation_id, optional), the receipt statuses and the block timestamps. All three are scheduled in one sitting and wait one delay: each execute timestamp is at least 172800 s after the same entry's schedule timestamp. No two entries share a transaction or an operation id. update-delay, batch and cancel are Twin-only and are rejected on 8453. Issue 1667: a vault that pause-all paused is reopened by a numbered Safe round; for a vault paused again, add a further entry of the same step with round 2, 3 and so on (each scheduled after the previous round executed, with its own transactions and operation id). A post-launch consensus receipt release (issue 1611, never part of stage 13) goes in receipt_releases, one entry per receipt id, with consensus_receipt.address: one schedule and one execute at least 172800 s apart, target the receipt contract, calldata releaseReceipt(receipt_id). Leave receipt_releases empty when none was released. A post-launch receipt application (issue 1696, govern --row apply-receipt, never part of stage 13) goes in receipt_applications with governance.address, one entry per receipt id: ONE timelock call, applyReceipt(receipt_id, payload_digest, vaults, bps) on the governance contract (the weight setter, issue 1698), which releases the receipt and sets the router active vector together; target is the governance contract, with the vault list (vaults), the weights (bps, summing to 10000), the payload digest, the operation id, both transactions, both statuses and both block timestamps at least 172800 s apart. Each entry also records the read-back after the execute (issue 1743): voted_weights_active true (the applied vector is the router active vector) and effective_vaults / effective_bps, the router getEffectiveWeights, equal to vaults / bps. Leave receipt_applications empty when none was applied. Issue 1988: nothing clears the router's active vector, so no tool writes voted_weights_clears (an older run manifest may hold historical entries). ADR-0017, issue 1912: the retirement of one vault (govern --row retire-vault, never part of stage 13) goes in vault_retirements with registry.address and timelock.address, one entry per round: ONE timelock batch of two calls, registry.migrateEligibility(vault, false, three legs) then registry.retire(vault), the retired vault (vault), the three-leg default vector that stays (vaults, bps, 10000 bps, the retired vault out), the operation id, both transactions, both statuses, both block timestamps at least 172800 s apart, the effective weights read back: voted_weights_active false and the effective weights equal to the vector, or voted_weights_active true with the applied vector that stays (issue 1988: its vaults without the retired one are the vector's, and retired_leg_skipped true while it still names the retired vault). Leave vault_retirements empty when none was run. Issue 1727: deployment_kind is production here (absent means production). A Base mainnet REHEARSAL (sheet DEPLOYMENT_KIND=rehearsal, a 900 s timelock) is checked with evidence-check --deployment-kind rehearsal: deployment_kind rehearsal, deployer_start_nonce (the nonce the run manifest recorded at the first stage), timelock.min_delay 900 to 172799, rehearsal_rows (update-delay, batch, cancel), submitter_registrations and recorded_receipts (issue 1888: in any kind, production included). submitter_registrations holds one entry per submitter Safe: ONE delayed timelock call, receipt.grantRole(RECEIPT_SUBMITTER_ROLE, submitter), with step register-submitter, submitter, receipt, timelock, operation_id, both transactions, both statuses, both block timestamps at least the delay floor apart, and submitter_safe (threshold 2 or more, owners, code_hash). recorded_receipts holds one entry per receipt the submitter Safe recorded directly on the receipt contract (id, digest, uri, submitter address, tx_hash, submitter_safe with the Safe transaction hash, nonce and signers; never a key); a single key is refused in every mode. HISTORICAL committee_registrations entries (step register-committee, the retired gateway batch of issues 1727 and 1750) of pinned releases still validate and a new run never writes them. Once RouterGovernance holds RECEIPT_RELEASER_ROLE, set consensus_receipt.governance_has_release_role to true (the timelock manifest's roles.governance_has_receipt_release_role): a standalone receipt_releases entry is then refused, because only apply-receipt releases. No secret goes in this file.

upgradeability._comment: Issue 1809: copy deployments/8453/upgradeability.json, which the verify stage writes from the chain, here unchanged (drop chain_id and core_sha). One entry per proxied core contract of the stage table (the ten: vault[rmUSDC], registry, router, gateway, icpolicy, receipt, governance, vault[rmPROTO], vault[rmAGENT], vault[rmRWA]): proxy and implementation addresses, both runtime code hashes, the storage layout file and its layout_id, upgrade_timelock, upgrades_frozen, initialized_version and manifest_upgrade_mode. mode is the sheet's UPGRADE_MODE; freeze_deadline is set only for an upgradeable release (required on a production one). core_immutable is true only for a frozen release whose full core set verified frozen with every check passing; otherwise immutability_refused_because says why. remaining_governed_parameters and upstream_dependencies are the verifier's lists of what a freeze does not make immutable. evidence-check reads every proxy fact back from the chain with --rpc or --chain-fixture.
